const ROOT = '/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon'
const PROJ = ROOT + '/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge'

const COMMON = `
You are auditing the Lean 4 project at ${PROJ} (package \`AlgebraicJacobian\`, Lean/Mathlib v4.31.0,
164 modules, ~122k lines). The workspace root is ${ROOT}.

HARD CONSTRAINTS FOR THIS PHASE:
- READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit, write, or create any file anywhere. Do NOT run \`lake build\`,

- Do not use the \`horizon\` CLI to WRITE anything. \`horizon roadmap list\`, \`horizon inbox list\`

- Every load-bearing claim must carry file:line evidence. Do not guess. If you did not verify

- Be exhaustive within your dimension; another agent covers each other dimension.

Useful context (already established, do not re-derive):
- 86 of the 164 modules contain a bare \`import Mathlib\` (the full umbrella).
- set_option inventory: 142 maxHeartbeats, 39 synthInstance.maxHeartbeats, 15 maxSynthPendingDepth,

  \`declaration uses sorry\`.
- The workspace ledger git is: git --git-dir ${ROOT}/.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git --work-tree ${ROOT}
`

const FINDINGS = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['dimension', 'headline', 'findings', 'recommended_actions'],
  properties: {
    dimension: { type: 'string' },
    headline: { type: 'string', description: 'One paragraph: the single most important thing found in this dimension.' },
    findings: {

      items: {

        required: ['title', 'evidence', 'impact', 'effort'],
        properties: {
          title: { type: 'string' },
          evidence: { type: 'string', description: 'file:line citations and measured counts' },
          impact: { type: 'string', enum: ['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low'] },
          effort: { type: 'string', enum: ['trivial', 'small', 'medium', 'large'] },
        },
      },
    },
    recommended_actions: {
      type: 'array',
      description: 'Concrete, ordered, mechanically executable work items a fixer agent could take verbatim.',
      items: {

        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['action', 'files', 'why', 'risk'],
        properties: {
          action: { type: 'string' },
          files: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
          why: { type: 'string' },
          risk: { type: 'string' },
        },
      },
    },
  },
}

const DIMENSIONS = [
  {
    key: 'imports',
    prompt: `${COMMON}
DIMENSION: IMPORT HYGIENE AND BUILD-GRAPH SHAPE. This is the highest-stakes dimension — the
user's headline complaint is a 6-hour from-scratch build.

Produce:
1. The exact list of the 86 modules with a bare \`import Mathlib\`, grouped by directory.
2. The project's internal import DAG: for each module, its project-internal imports. Identify
   (a) the leaf/root modules (imported by nobody but the umbrella \`AlgebraicJacobian.lean\`),
   (b) the highest-fan-in modules, (c) the longest dependency chain (critical path length) — a
   from-scratch parallel build cannot be faster than its critical path.
3. Which modules already use precise Mathlib imports (a good in-repo template to copy).
4. Modules with duplicate/redundant imports (a module importing both X and something that
   already imports X *inside this project*), and modules importing project modules they do not
   use (grep the file body for names declared in the imported module; report only high-confidence
   cases).
5. Whether \`Mathlib.Tactic.Linter.MinImports\` (the \`linter.minImports\` option) and the
   \`#min_imports in\` command exist in the pinned mathlib at
   ${ROOT}/.lake-packages/mathlib — quote the declaration sites. Write the exact incantation a
   fixer would use to compute a minimal import set for one file, and any known caveat (e.g. it
   reports imports needed for the syntax elaborated *so far*, tactic imports it can miss).
6. A concrete, ORDERED de-umbrella plan: which modules to convert first so the win propagates
   (a module only stops paying for \`import Mathlib\` when NO module in its transitive project
   import closure imports the umbrella — so order matters, bottom-up from the DAG sources).
   State explicitly how many modules must be converted before ANY module sees a win.
7. The root aggregator ${PROJ}/AlgebraicJacobian.lean: is it well-formed, sorted, complete?
   Are there .lean files under AlgebraicJacobian/ NOT reachable from it?`,
  },
  {
    key: 'budgets',
    prompt: `${COMMON}
DIMENSION: ELABORATION RESOURCE BUDGETS (\`set_option\` overrides). The user explicitly
complained "there are heartbeat everywhere".

Produce a complete inventory table. For EVERY \`set_option maxHeartbeats\`,
\`set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats\`, \`set_option maxSynthPendingDepth\`,
\`set_option maxRecDepth\`, and \`set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false\` scope
in ${PROJ}/AlgebraicJacobian, record: file, line, value, the declaration it wraps (name and
kind), whether it is \`... in\` (scoped to one declaration) or file-scoped (dangerous — it
silently applies to everything below), and whether a comment immediately above it documents a
measured rationale.

Then:
1. Rank files by total override count and by aggregate "excess" (sum of value/200000).
2. Flag every FILE-SCOPED (non-\`in\`) budget override — these are the worst offenders because
   they mask cost for all following declarations. Give exact file:line.
3. Flag the extreme sites (>= 3200000 heartbeats) individually with the wrapped declaration name.
4. Explain what \`backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false\` does in Lean 4.31 (read the option
   declaration in ${ROOT}/.lake-packages/mathlib or the Lean source under
   ${ROOT}/.lake-packages/ if present; if you cannot find it, say so). Assess whether 289
   occurrences is a design smell and what the idiomatic alternative is. Are they file-scoped or
   \`in\`-scoped? Do any wrap a whole file?
5. Propose a REMOVAL TEST PROTOCOL that a later fixer agent can run per file with a single
   targeted \`lake build\` of that module's target, and a priority order (cheapest modules and
   most-likely-obsolete scopes first). Take account of the fact that lowering a budget is a
   partial win when removal fails.
6. Identify scopes that are provably obsolete: e.g. a budget on a declaration whose proof is now
   one line, or duplicated adjacent identical scopes that could be one \`section\`-level
   \`set_option ... in\` — but be careful, per-declaration \`in\` scoping is the mathlib
   convention and is PREFERRED over file-scope.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'warnings',
    prompt: `${COMMON}
DIMENSION: LEAN WARNINGS. A full warm build log with every warning is at
/tmp/ajc-warm-build.log (162 warning heads; lines start with "warning: "). Read it.

Produce a per-file, per-warning worklist covering ALL 138 non-\`sorry\` warnings:
file, line:col, warning category, the offending source text (read it from the file), and the
EXACT minimal edit that fixes it. Categories observed: \`show\` tactic used to change the goal
(fix: \`change\`), unused variable name / unused section variable / unused hypothesis in type,
unused simp argument, line over 100 chars, overlapping instance parameters, deprecated API
(name the replacement, verified against mathlib source), \`simpa\` that should be \`simp\`,
"flexible tactic" linter, missing space, copyright-header linter complaints, and
"Definition of class type must be marked with instance".

For each of the 4 header-linter complaints (they look like \`* '-/':\` and
\`* 'hallenge contributors.':\`), read the actual file header and state the exact required
mathlib copyright-header shape and what is wrong.

Also list the 24 \`declaration uses sorry\` sites with the declaration name and the file, so the
roadmap can present them as the honest remaining-work list. Do NOT propose removing them.

Group the worklist into per-file batches sized so one fixer agent can own a file end-to-end.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'conventions',
    prompt: `${COMMON}
DIMENSION: MATHLIB CONVENTIONS AND CODE QUALITY (beyond what the linters already flag).

Compare this project against mathlib's own style, using the pinned mathlib at
${ROOT}/.lake-packages/mathlib as the reference (read real mathlib files to justify claims).
Assess and give file:line evidence for:
1. Module headers: does each file have the mathlib copyright block + a \`# Title\` module
   docstring with "## Main results" / "## References"? How many of the 164 do not? List the worst.
2. Declaration docstrings on public defs/theorems: coverage estimate, worst files.
3. Naming: do declaration names follow mathlib's naming convention (lowerCamelCase for data,
   snake_case-of-symbol-names for proofs, namespace discipline)? Sample at least 40 declarations
   across different files and report violations concretely.
4. Namespace hygiene: are declarations put in \`AlgebraicGeometry\`/\`Mathlib\` namespaces where
   they would collide with mathlib, or in a project namespace? Any declarations that shadow or
   duplicate an existing mathlib lemma (use \`horizon search\` read-only, and grep mathlib)?
   Report suspected duplicates with both names.
5. Proof style: \`sorry\`-free \`private\` helper duplication across files (the same helper lemma
   restated in several modules) — this workspace has been bitten by that before; find repeated
   lemma statements with different names.
6. Anti-patterns: \`native_decide\`, \`decide\` on big goals, \`omega\`/\`simp\` misuse, very long
   single proofs (report the 15 longest declarations by line count with file:line),
   very long files (report files over 2000 lines), and deeply nested \`obtain\`/\`have\` chains.
7. Anything a mathlib reviewer would reject on sight.

Prioritize findings that also make the build faster or the file easier to maintain.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'blueprint',
    prompt: `${COMMON}
DIMENSION: BLUEPRINT. Sources at ${PROJ}/blueprint. First read the house rules:
${ROOT}/.claude/skills/blueprint-conventions/SKILL.md (read it in full, it is binding).

Produce:
1. The chapter inventory: file, line count, and a one-line description of what it covers.
2. VIOLATIONS OF THE MATH-PURITY RULE: every place where blueprint prose is a formalization
   journal rather than timeless mathematics — "we tried", "Lean", "the current Lean file",
   "iteration", "TODO", "note that the proof below is a stub", route comparisons, status
   reports, dates, agent/session references. Give file:line and quote the offending text.
   Prior sessions flagged RelPicFunctor and IdentityComponent specifically — verify and go wider.
3. Incomplete proofs: \`\\begin{proof}\` bodies that are sketches ("clear", "standard",
   "omitted", "see [ref]", one-liners with no argument) where the house rules demand a complete
   proof. Give file:line.
4. \`\\lean{...}\` pins: sample at least 30 and check the named Lean declaration actually exists
   in ${PROJ}/AlgebraicJacobian (grep for it). Report every dangling pin.
5. \`\\leanok\` claims on nodes whose Lean declaration contains \`sorry\` (transitively is fine to
   skip; direct \`sorry\` in the declaration body is the check). Report every false \`\\leanok\`.
6. \`\\uses{...}\` references to labels that do not exist; and labels declared twice.
7. \`\\source{...}\` anchors: how many nodes cite a source, how many do not; which chapters are
   worst.
8. Structural cleanliness: chapter ordering, duplicated material across chapters, dead/unused
   \`.tex\` files not \\input from the main file, and whether the main file is tidy.
Rank by what most damages a reader's trust in the blueprint.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'roadmap',
    prompt: `${COMMON}
DIMENSION: ROADMAP STRUCTURE. The user asked, verbatim: "I first want ... the roadmap to be
refactored to be cleaner (using subitems etc) showing clearly what's been done and what's still
to be done. In the current roadmap all the already done items (like sheafs, schemes, etc, etc)
should all be represented with done label, so that it is easier to follow up the real progress."

Read (read-only):
- \`${ROOT}/.archon-horizon/roadmap/\` on disk (find the item files and read them directly — this
  is faster and more complete than the CLI), and/or
  \`/home/axel/.archon-env/bin/horizon roadmap list --root ${ROOT} --json\`
- ${ROOT}/roadmap.md
- ${PROJ}/README.md, ${PROJ}/TO_USER.md

Produce:
1. The complete current AJC-relevant roadmap tree with statuses (ids, titles, status, parent).
2. TOP-LEVEL ORPHANS: nodes \`CECH.*\`, \`GRQ.*\`, \`LBC.*\`, \`ALB.*\`, \`PIC.*\`, \`MR.*\` sit at the
   roadmap root although the roadmap.md says Cech-Cohomology, GR-Quot-Closure and
   Line-Bundle-Comparison-Iso were MERGED into Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge. Determine, with
   evidence, which of these belong nested under \`AJC.jacobian\` and which are genuinely separate
   projects. Propose the exact re-parenting.
3. COMPLETED-BUT-UNMARKED WORK: cross-check the roadmap against reality. For each major theme
   the project has actually finished (sheaf/scheme substrate, line bundles, Cech engine,
   Grassmannian/Quot H0 leg, graded Hilbert-Serre, glue descent, relative Spec, flattening
   stratification, generic flatness, adelic Riemann-Roch genus, rigidity, Auslander-Buchsbaum,
   ...), find whether a roadmap node exists and whether it is marked \`done\`. Where a finished
   theme has NO node, propose the node to add (id, title, parent, one-sentence summary) so the
   user can see the real progress. Verify "finished" by checking the Lean modules for \`sorry\`
   (a theme is done iff its modules have no direct \`sorry\`); cite the modules.
4. The honest remaining-work tree: for each of the 24 \`sorry\` sites, which roadmap leaf covers
   it. Report sorries with no covering leaf.
5. A proposed FINAL roadmap shape for AJC: a clean 2-4 level outline where every leaf is either
   \`done\` or names a concrete open obligation, plus the exact ordered list of
   \`horizon roadmap add/set --parent ...\` commands that would produce it. Keep ids stable where
   they already exist; only propose renames when the current id is actively misleading.
Be concrete: your output will be executed nearly verbatim.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'deadcode',
    prompt: `${COMMON}
DIMENSION: DEAD CODE, ORPHANS, AND REPOSITORY TIDINESS.

1. Every .lean file under ${PROJ}/AlgebraicJacobian that is NOT in the transitive import closure
   of ${PROJ}/AlgebraicJacobian.lean. (Parse the import lines; a module is reachable iff some
   reachable module imports it.) This workspace has been bitten by "a module with no importer
   looks green and is invisible" — take it seriously and give the exact list.
2. Declarations that are declared but never used anywhere in the project AND not plausibly part
   of the public API (be conservative: only report clear cases such as private helpers with zero
   references). Use grep counts as evidence.
3. \`${PROJ}/analogies/\`: 123 historical design notes. Read analogies/README.md and sample ~15
   files. Classify: which contain a durable mathematical or API lesson worth keeping, which are
   superseded iteration journals safe to retire. Propose a consolidation (e.g. keep N, fold the
   rest into one index with one-line summaries, or delete). Give the concrete list.
4. \`${PROJ}/informal/\`, \`${PROJ}/memory/\`, \`${PROJ}/archon/\`: what is in them, is any of it
   live state or all stale? Propose action.
5. Stray build/temp artifacts committed into the tree; files in .gitignore that are tracked
   anyway; anything large and useless.
6. ${PROJ}/README.md and TO_USER.md accuracy: check every factual claim against the tree and
   report the false ones.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'sorries',
    prompt: `${COMMON}
DIMENSION: THE HONEST REMAINING-WORK LIST.

Find every direct \`sorry\` in ${PROJ}/AlgebraicJacobian (strip comments and docstrings first —
write a small python3 script that removes \`--\` line comments and \`/- ... -/\` block comments,
then finds \`sorry\` tokens; do NOT trust a naive grep, which reports 261 hits against a true
count near 24).

For each real \`sorry\`:
- file:line, the enclosing declaration's full name and statement (quote the statement),
- a one-sentence statement of the MATHEMATICAL obligation in plain prose,
- what it blocks downstream (grep for uses of the declaration),
- whether the statement looks correct as stated (flag anything suspicious, e.g. missing
  hypotheses, a \`Prop\` with no producer, a definition that is \`sorry\`ed rather than a proof —
  a \`sorry\`ed *definition* is much worse than a \`sorry\`ed proof, call those out loudly).

Also find other forms of incompleteness that a naive sorry-count misses:
- \`axiom\` declarations added by this project (grep \`^axiom\`), and \`@[implemented_by]\`,
  \`native_decide\`, \`Classical.choice\`-shaped escapes,
- declarations whose statement is trivially true / vacuous (e.g. \`True\`, \`Nonempty\` of
  something with no content, a \`Prop\` field that is never inhabited),
- \`sorry\`-free but STUB definitions: defs whose body is \`Classical.choice\`, \`default\`,
  \`⊥\`, or an arbitrary element, standing in for real content.
Report anything that makes the project look more complete than it is. This is a truth audit;
err toward reporting.`,
  },
]

  DIMENSIONS,
  d => agent(d.prompt, { label: `audit:${d.key}`, phase: 'Audit', schema: FINDINGS }),

produced the report below. Your job is to REFUTE it: find claims that are wrong, counts that are
off, file:line citations that do not say what is claimed, recommendations that would break the
build or the mathematics, and important things the auditor MISSED in its own dimension.

Same hard constraints: READ-ONLY, no Lean processes, no lake, no edits.

Check at minimum: every numeric count (recount it yourself), a random sample of at least 8
file:line citations, and every recommendation marked risk-free. Default to "refuted" when you
cannot confirm a load-bearing claim.

REPORT UNDER AUDIT:
${JSON.stringify(res, null, 1).slice(0, 60000)}`, {
      label: `verify:${d.key}`,
      phase: 'Verify',
      schema: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['dimension', 'verdict', 'corrections', 'missed', 'trustworthy_actions'],
        properties: {
          dimension: { type: 'string' },
          verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['sound', 'mostly-sound-with-corrections', 'unreliable'] },
          corrections: {
            type: 'array',
            items: {
              type: 'object',
              additionalProperties: false,
              required: ['claim', 'why_wrong', 'correct_version'],
              properties: {
                claim: { type: 'string' },
                why_wrong: { type: 'string' },
                correct_version: { type: 'string' },
              },
            },
          },
          missed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
          trustworthy_actions: {
            type: 'array',
            description: 'The recommended actions from the report that survived verification, restated precisely and safely, most valuable first.',
            items: { type: 'string' },
          },
        },
      },
    }).then(v => ({ dimension: d.key, audit: res, verification: v }))
  },
)

return results.filter(Boolean)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Parse a timestamped `lake build -v` log into a per-module elaboration profile.

Each log line is `<epoch>|<text>`.  Job starts appear as
`trace: .> LEAN_PATH=... lean <abs path to .lean> -o <...>.olean ...`
and job ends as `... ] Built <Module.Name>`.
"""
import re
import sys
from collections import OrderedDict

path = sys.argv[1]
prefix = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "AlgebraicJacobian"

start = {}
end = {}
t0 = None
tlast = None

lean_re = re.compile(r"lean (\S+\.lean) -o (\S+\.olean)")
built_re = re.compile(r"\] Built (\S+)")

with open(path, errors="replace") as fh:
    for line in fh:
        ts, _, text = line.partition("|")
        try:
            t = float(ts)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if t0 is None:
            t0 = t
        tlast = t
        m = lean_re.search(text)
        if m:
            olean = m.group(2)
            # module name from the olean path segment after build/lib/lean/
            mm = re.search(r"/build/lib/lean/(.+)\.olean$", olean)
            if mm:
                mod = mm.group(1).replace("/", ".")
                start.setdefault(mod, t)
            continue
        m = built_re.search(text)
        if m:
            end[m.group(1)] = t

rows = []
for mod, t_end in end.items():
    if not mod.startswith(prefix):
        continue
    t_start = start.get(mod)
    if t_start is None:
        continue
    rows.append((t_end - t_start, mod, t_start - t0, t_end - t0))

rows.sort(reverse=True)
total_serial = sum(r[0] for r in rows)
print(f"# modules built: {len(rows)}   wall so far: {tlast - t0:.0f}s   "
      f"serial CPU sum: {total_serial:.0f}s   speedup: {total_serial / max(tlast - t0, 1):.1f}x")
print(f"{'secs':>7}  {'start':>7}  {'end':>7}  module")
for dur, mod, s, e in rows:
    print(f"{dur:7.1f}  {s:7.0f}  {e:7.0f}  {mod}")

3	description: The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
4	---
5	
6	Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
7	Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.
8	
9	## Environments
10	
11	Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
12	`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
13	`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
14	its following `proof` environment form one node's content.
15	
16	## Per-node macros
17	
18	- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
19	- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration(s) this node formalizes; comma-separate to
20	  bind several (`\lean{a, b}`) when they jointly formalize the node's statement.
21	  Each named declaration's signature must match the statement. The mapping need
22	  not be 1-to-1: a node may name several declarations, and Lean may carry
23	  auxiliary declarations with no node at all.
24	- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
25	  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
26	  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
27	  proof.
28	- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
29	  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
30	  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
31	- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
32	  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
33	  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
34	- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
35	  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).
36	
37	## House style
38	
39	- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
40	  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
41	  and no conversational filler. Not every Lean helper needs its own node —
42	  auxiliary or implementation-only declarations can stay unnoded; add a node when
43	  the result is mathematically meaningful in its own right. In particular, never
44	  add a `Formalization note` paragraph to blueprint `.tex`: attach implementation
45	  details, failed approaches, and mechanization caveats to the statement's hgraph
46	  node with `horizon graph ... add comment` instead.
47	- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
48	  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
49	  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
50	  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
51	  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
52	  its proof stays complete.
53	- **One statement's worth per node.** Keep each node to a single mathematical
54	  statement; don't restate Lean source as prose.
55	- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
56	  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
57	  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
58	  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

rootfile='AlgebraicJacobian.lean'
rootdeps=[]
for line in open(rootfile):
    m=re.match(r'^import\s+([A-Za-z0-9_.]+)',line)
    if m and m.group(1).startswith('AlgebraicJacobian'): rootdeps.append(m.group(1))
print('root aggregator imports:',len(rootdeps))
seen=set()
stack=list(rootdeps)
while stack:
    x=stack.pop()
    if x in seen: continue
    seen.add(x)
    stack.extend(imports.get(x,[]))
orphans=sorted(set(mods)-seen)
print('unreachable modules:',len(orphans))
for o in orphans: print('   ',o)
missing=[d for d in rootdeps if d not in mods]
print('root imports naming nonexistent modules:',missing)
# transitive umbrella contamination
memo={}
def contaminated(m):
    if m in memo: return memo[m]
    memo[m]=True # cycle guard
    r = m in umbrella or any(contaminated(d) for d in imports.get(m,[]))
    memo[m]=r
    return r
cont=[m for m in mods if contaminated(m)]
print('modules transitively importing Mathlib umbrella:',len(cont),'/',len(mods))
clean=sorted(set(mods)-set(cont))
print('umbrella-free modules:',len(clean))
for c in clean[:40]: print('   clean:',c)
# fan-in
fanin=collections.Counter()
for m,ds in imports.items():
    for d in ds: fanin[d]+=1
print('\ntop fan-in:')
for m,c in fanin.most_common(15): print(f'  {c:4d}  {m}')
# critical path (longest chain by module count)
depth={}
def dep(m):
    if m in depth: return depth[m]
    depth[m]=0
    v=1+max([dep(d) for d in imports.get(m,[])]+[0])
    depth[m]=v
    return v
mx=max(mods,key=dep)

# reconstruct
chain=[mx]
cur=mx
while imports.get(cur):
    cur=max(imports[cur],key=dep)
    chain.append(cur)

It returns the modules that are transitively imported by `ms`, using the data in `tc`.

def importsBelow (tc : NameMap NameSet) (ms : NameSet) : NameSet :=
  ms.foldl (·.append <| tc.getD · default) ms

@[inherit_doc Mathlib.Linter.linter.minImports]
macro "#import_bumps" : command => `(
  -- We emit a message to prevent the `#`-command linter from flagging `#import_bumps`.
  run_cmd logInfo "Counting imports from here."
  set_option Elab.async false
  set_option linter.minImports true)

@[inherit_doc Mathlib.Linter.linter.minImports]
def minImportsLinter : Linter where run := withSetOptionIn fun stx ↦ do
    unless getLinterValue linter.minImports (← getLinterOptions) do
      return
    if (← get).messages.hasErrors then
      return
    if stx == (← `(command| #import_bumps)) then return
    if stx == (← `(command| set_option $(mkIdent `linter.minImports) true)) then
      logInfo "Try using '#import_bumps', instead of manually setting the linter option: \
              the linter works best with linear parsing of the file and '#import_bumps' \
              also sets the `Elab.async` option to `false`."
      return
    let env ← getEnv
    -- the first time `minImportsRef` is read, it has `transClosure = none`;
    -- in this case, we set it to be the `transClosure` for the file.
    if (← minImportsRef.get).transClosure.isNone then
      minImportsRef.modify ({· with transClosure := env.importGraph.transitiveClosure})
    let impState ← minImportsRef.get
    let (importsSoFar, oldCumulImps) := (impState.minImports, impState.importSize)
    -- when the linter reaches the end of the file or `#exit`, it gives a report
    if #[``Parser.Command.eoi, ``Lean.Parser.Command.exit].contains stx.getKind then
      let explicitImportsInFile : NameSet :=
        .ofArray ((env.imports.map (·.module)).filter (!isInitImport ·))
      let newImps := importsSoFar \ explicitImportsInFile
      let currentlyUnneededImports := explicitImportsInFile \ importsSoFar
      -- we read the current file, to do a custom parsing of the imports:
      -- this is a hack to obtain some `Syntax` information for the `import X` commands
      let fname ← getFileName
      let contents ← IO.FS.readFile fname
      -- `impMods` is the syntax for the modules imported in the current file
      let (impMods, _) ← Parser.parseHeader (Parser.mkInputContext contents fname)
      for i in currentlyUnneededImports do
        match impMods.raw.find? (·.getId == i) with
          | some impPos => logWarningAt impPos m!"unneeded import '{i}'"
          | _ => dbg_trace f!"'{i}' not found"  -- this should be unreachable
      -- if the linter found new imports that should be added (likely to *reduce* the dependencies)
      if !newImps.isEmpty then
        -- format the imports prepending `import ` to each module name
        let withImport := (newImps.toArray.qsort Name.lt).map (s!"import {·}")
        -- log a warning at the first `import`, if there is one.
        logWarningAt ((impMods.raw.find? (·.isOfKind `import)).getD default)
          m!"-- missing imports\n{"\n".intercalate withImport.toList}"
    let id ← getId stx
    let newImports := (getIrredundantImports env (← getAllImports stx id)).filter (!isInitImport ·)
    let tot := (newImports.append importsSoFar)
    let redundant := env.findRedundantImports tot.toArray
    let currImports := tot \ redundant
    let currImpArray := currImports.toArray.qsort Name.lt
    if currImpArray != #[] &&
       currImpArray ≠ importsSoFar.toArray.qsort Name.lt then
      let newCumulImps := -- We should always be in the situation where `getD` finds something
        (importsBelow (impState.transClosure.getD env.importGraph.transitiveClosure) tot).size
      minImportsRef.modify ({· with minImports := currImports, importSize := newCumulImps})
      let new := currImpArray.filter (!importsSoFar.contains ·)
      let redundant := importsSoFar.toArray.filter (!currImports.contains ·)
      -- to make `test` files more stable, we suppress the exact count of import changes if
      -- the `linter.minImports.increases` option is `false`
      let byCount :=  if getLinterValue linter.minImports.increases (← getLinterOptions) then

        m!"Imports increased {byCount}to\n{currImpArray}\n\n\
          New imports: {new}\n" ++
            if redundant.isEmpty then m!"" else m!"\nNow redundant: {redundant}\n"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Compute the minimal Mathlib import set for one module of this package.
#
#   scripts/min-imports.sh AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Foo.lean [outdir]
#
# Uses Mathlib's `#import_bumps` (the `linter.minImports` linter).  The linter
# reports, at end of file, both the imports that are missing and the declared
# imports that are unneeded.  We run it on a copy in $outdir so the real source
# is never touched and Lake's build products stay valid.
#
# Output on stdout, machine readable:
#   MISSING <module>       (one per line, an import to add)
#   UNNEEDED <module>      (one per line, a declared import that is not needed)
#   STATUS ok|error
#
# The raw Lean output is left in $outdir/<basename>.out for inspection.
set -uo pipefail

SRC=${1:?usage: min-imports.sh <file.lean> [outdir]}
OUT=${2:-/tmp/ajc-minimports}
mkdir -p "$OUT"

base=$(basename "$SRC" .lean)
tmp="$OUT/$base.probe.lean"
raw="$OUT/$base.out"

# Insert `#import_bumps` immediately after the final import line.
python3 - "$SRC" "$tmp" <<'PY'
import sys
src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
lines = open(src, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
last = -1
for i, l in enumerate(lines):

Base directory for this skill: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/project-git

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.
